title: Dhirubhai Ambani: From a Job in Yemen to Reliance
description:
Reliance Industries brought in ₹11.76 lakh crore (about $124 billion) in FY2025-26. Its founder, Dhirubhai Ambani, left India at 17 for Aden, in today's Yemen, where obituaries say he worked at a petrol station and then as a clerk (accounts of these early details vary). Back in Mumbai he traded yarn and spices, and in 1977 took Reliance public: a ₹2.8 crore (₹28 million) issue oversubscribed seven times. His methods also drew criticism, reported by Reuters at his death in 2002. (1 crore = 10 million; 1 lakh crore = 1 trillion.)

Sources: Reliance Industries Q4 FY2025-26 media release (24 Apr 2026); RIL 'Our history' (ril.com); Business Standard (7 Jun 2012) on the 1977 issue; Reuters obituary via Dawn (8 Jul 2002); Voice of America (7 Jul 2002); Encyclopaedia Britannica. Educational content, not investment advice.

scenes.say: Over eleven lakh crore rupees a year. Its founder started in Yemen.
At seventeen, Dhirubhai Ambani left India for Aden, in today's Yemen.
Obituaries say he worked at a petrol station, then as a clerk.
Back in Mumbai, he traded yarn and spices. At forty-four, he took Reliance public.
That nineteen seventy-seven I-P-O raised two point eight crore rupees, oversubscribed seven times.
But here's the catch: there's another side.
Reuters reported accusations his success owed as much to policy manipulation as business skill.
The lesson: think big and bring investors along. But how you win matters.
